newsitem.title: RUSSIA: NORDIC SKIING-RUSSIANS CONDEMN YEGOROVA FOR DOPING.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-RUSSIANS CONDEMN YEGOROVA FOR DOPING.

text.p: Lyubov Yegorova's Russian team mates said they were surprised and disappointed after she admitted taking the banned drug Bromantan before a gold-medal performance at the Nordic skiing world championships.

Alexander Grishun, head coach of the Russian women's team, said on Thursday Yegorova, six times an Olympic champion and three times a world champion, was finished in the sport and had no chance of being picked for next year's Nagano Olympics.
"I fear that she'll have to accept she is finished with the Olympics and with skiing in general," he said.
Top Russian skiing administrator Viktor Mamatov added:"I'm very sorry this case has cast a shadow not only over Yegorova but on the winning performances of her team mates.

The 30-year-old former world champion's admission was a big embarrassment for Russian sports so soon after controversy over the use of the same substance by some Russian athletes at last year's Atlanta Olympics.

Yelena Vialbe, awarded the gold after coming second to her Russian team mate in Sunday's 5-km classic cross-country race, said Yegorova's disqualification had spoiled her own triumphs, including two other golds this week.
"I haven't slept for two nights," she said.
"After what happened with Bromantan in Atlanta she should have known not to take those pills. Now I feel no joy at my own medals. It's very unpleasant."
The entire Russian team demanded that Yegorova leave the Trondheim championships in Norway immediately, said the vice-president of the Russian Ski Federation, Boris Bystrov.
Yegorova claimed ignorance caused her to take the pills.
She told Russia's Sport Express newspaper she had reached "automatically" for an old pack of Bromantan she had had since she won three golds at the 1994 Lillehammer Olympics.
"I didn't understand the substance was banned," she said, explaining she had been in hospital during the Atlanta games.
"You'd have to be suicidal to take Bromantan knowing it was banned," Yegorova added. "Believe me, I really didn't know. It's a nightmare to get caught for such a trifle."
